content.label: Examiner note - dot-and-cross is bookkeeping
content.body: The dots and crosses only record which atom each electron came from - both electrons in the shared pair are shared equally once the bond exists, and nothing becomes charged. Draw the outer shells only, and every atom must end at a noble-gas count (hydrogen at 2). One shared pair is a single bond; two pairs make the double bond in O2 or CO2.
